name: Alaska
statusNote: Adult-use legal since the 2014 initiative; stores opened in 2016.
outlook: Stable adult-use market. New Democratic governor and Senate seat flip add pro-reform voices in Washington.

name: Alabama
statusNote: Medical law (2021); first dispensary opened June 2026.
outlook: Medical market finally live and slowly expanding; adult-use not on the agenda.

name: Arkansas
outlook: No major 2026 movement found; Republican trifecta makes adult-use unlikely near term.

name: Arizona
outlook: Repeal threat faded in May 2026 when its sponsor dropped the initiative.

name: California
outlook: DEA says it cannot register California medical dispensaries under current state law; watch for state fixes.

name: Colorado
outlook: Mature market; revised marijuana rules took effect Nov 1, 2026.

name: Connecticut
regulator: Dept. of Consumer Protection / Social Equity Council
outlook: 2026 session made the biggest changes since legalization; hemp rules tighten Dec 1, 2026.

name: District of Columbia
statusNote: Possession legal (Initiative 71); commercial adult-use sales blocked by a congressional rider.
outlook: Included for completeness. DEA rejected DC medical registrations in November.

name: Delaware
outlook: Young market working through social-equity licensing problems.

name: Florida
outlook: Governor-elect opposes recreational; 2026 initiative failed to qualify. Medical market tightening.

name: Georgia
statusNote: Became a comprehensive medical state with SB 220 (signed May 12, 2026).
regulator: Georgia Access to Medical Cannabis Commission
outlook: Medical program now much broader; new Democratic governor-elect, Republican legislature.

name: Hawaii
outlook: 2026 adult-use and constitutional-amendment bills did not pass; likely back in 2027.

name: Iowa
statusNote: Limited low-THC medical program (Iowa Code ch. 124E): licensed dispensaries, generally up to 4.5 g THC per 90 days; a 2026 law doubled dispensaries.
outlook: Governor-elect Sand wants to legalize and tax like alcohol; legislature is the gate.

name: Idaho
outlook: Voters rejected HJR 4 (66%), keeping the initiative route open; medical advocates eye 2028.

name: Illinois
outlook: State leaders want the federal hemp ban to proceed; state hemp rules tied up in court.

name: Indiana
outlook: Gov. Braun now open to medical; Sen. Bohacek plans a 2027 medical bill.

name: Kansas
outlook: Governor-elect supports legalization; Republican legislature remains the barrier.

name: Kentucky
outlook: Program scaling fast (30,000+ cardholders). Beshear pressing Congress on banking.

name: Louisiana
outlook: 2026 session raised penalties near schools while allowing hospital use for terminal patients.

name: Massachusetts
outlook: Voters crushed repeal (Question 8, ~76% no). Regulators active on testing and veterans access.

name: Maryland
outlook: Gov. Moore leading governors' push for SAFE Banking; hemp now flowing into dispensaries.

name: Maine
outlook: Repeal initiative failed to qualify; new senator-elect Troy Jackson backs reform.

name: Michigan
outlook: Industry adjusting to the new 24% wholesale tax.

name: Minnesota
outlook: Governor-elect Klobuchar is also leading a Senate push to save hemp THC products.

name: Missouri
outlook: New state hemp-THC limits in force; AG suing unlicensed sellers.

name: Mississippi
outlook: Stable medical program; Senate seat flipped to Democrat Scott Colom.

name: Montana
regulator: Dept. of Revenue – Cannabis Control Division
outlook: No major 2026 policy shifts found.

name: North Carolina
outlook: Democrats' new House leadership puts decriminalization and medical on the 2027 table.

name: North Dakota
statusNote: Medical program (2016); voters rejected adult-use in 2024.
outlook: Incremental medical tweaks only; adult-use failed three times at the ballot.

name: Nebraska
statusNote: Voter-approved 2024; regulations adopted July 2026; no patient sales yet.
outlook: Rule amendments now with the AG; no timeline yet for product testing or patient access.

name: New Hampshire
statusNote: Therapeutic Cannabis Program; only New England state without adult-use.
outlook: Democrats now control both chambers; Ayotte opposes, so a veto override is the path.

name: New Jersey
outlook: Gov. Sherrill signed a law aligning state hemp rules with federal policy.

name: New Mexico
outlook: Stable market; incoming governor Haaland.

name: Nevada
outlook: Governor-elect Ford sat on the state Cannabis Advisory Commission as AG.

name: New York
outlook: Licensing still expanding (nursery licenses opened Nov 2026).

name: Ohio
statusNote: Adult-use legal (Issue 2, 2023); rewritten by SB 56 (effective Mar 20, 2026).
outlook: Hemp-drink sales window under SB 56 closes Dec 31, 2026.

name: Oklahoma
outlook: Outgoing Gov. Stitt wanted a repeal vote; legislative leaders declined. Court reopened petition path.

name: Oregon
outlook: Mature market; local rule changes in Portland.

name: Pennsylvania
regulator: Pa. Dept. of Health – Medical Marijuana Program
outlook: Democrats flipped the Senate 26–24; legalization likely in 2027 but not the top priority.

name: Rhode Island
outlook: Regulators proposing operational and testing changes.

name: South Carolina
statusNote: No medical program in operation; Compassionate Care Act died May 2026.
outlook: Senate seat flipped to Democrat Annie Andrews; medical bill will return in 2027.

name: South Dakota
outlook: Legislature rejected 2026 bills to dismantle the medical program.

name: Tennessee
outlook: Advisory commission meets Nov 20; legislature remains opposed.

name: Texas
statusNote: Limited low-THC medical program (TCUP), expanded 2025; hemp THC widely sold.
outlook: Democratic governor, Lt. Gov. and AG-elects favor regulating hemp THC; 2027 session is pivotal.

name: Utah
regulator: Utah Center for Medical Cannabis (moving to UDAF)
outlook: Program oversight moves to the Agriculture Department by Jan 1, 2027.

name: Virginia
statusNote: Possession legal since 2021; retail sales begin July 1, 2027.
outlook: Retail law signed June 2026; legislators already recommending changes for 2027.

name: Vermont
outlook: Cannabis event permits now open.

name: Washington
outlook: Regulators proposing rules on financial interests and producer co-ops.

name: Wisconsin
outlook: Democrats won the governorship and both chambers; leaders say legalization will pass in 2027.

name: West Virginia
outlook: Stable medical program; ag commissioner urging Congress to regulate hemp instead of banning it.

name: Wyoming
outlook: No reform momentum found.
